earliestResponsibleBranch.branch: the NUMBERED_CAPTION_RE arm of the caption test (noInternalTerminator && (ALLCAPS || NUMBERED))
earliestResponsibleBranch.trace: segmentSourceUnits splits at line breaks, so 6.02 is its own unit -> the extractor finds no values in it -> no inventory span covers it -> classifyUnaccountedFragment runs -> pagination, citation and quoted-label rules decline -> contentWords is non-empty so STRUCTURAL_NOISE declines -> the caption test fires and returns HEADING_OR_LABEL. It is the first branch to grant an accounted disposition.

rootCause: NUMBERED_CAPTION_RE was /^\s*(?:section|article|annex|exhibit|schedule|appendix)?\s*\d+(?:\.\d+)*\s*[.:)]?\s*[A-Za-z][\w\s,'&/-]{0,80}?\s*[.:]?\s*$/i. Its body was an ARBITRARY RUN OF WORDS UNDER A LENGTH CEILING. Caption-hood was inferred from three things that prove nothing: a leading section number, the absence of an internal clause terminator, and being short enough. What actually follows the number was never examined. The red team measured the boundary at ~80 characters of body - a length ceiling deciding eligibility for scrutiny.

genericRuleImplemented.invariant: NUMBERING DOES NOT MAKE TEXT A CAPTION. A numbered line is a caption only when what FOLLOWS the number is itself a label; otherwise it is accountable source.
genericRuleImplemented.mechanism: NUMBERED_CAPTION_RE became NUMBERED_CAPTION_FRAME_RE, which matches only the numbering frame and captures the remainder. The remainder is put to isNominalLabel - the same positive structural test canary #5 introduced for the text inside quotation marks, reused unchanged rather than duplicated. Both frames pose the same question and neither frame answers it: quotes do not make text a name, and neither does a section number.
isNominalLabel: 1. No clause punctuation inside (. ; : ! ? ,) - sentence structure, which a name has none of.
2. Every word is either pure grammar (the existing FUNCTION_WORDS closed class) or an orthographic proper-noun form, and at least one is a name.
genericRuleImplemented.whyThisIsNotAVerbList: Nothing enumerates shall / may / must / incur / pay / make / maintain / permit / restrict, and no covenant-family pattern exists. A proposition is rejected because it carries a LOWERCASE CONTENT WORD acting as its predicate - 'shall', 'create', 'must', 'deliver', 'maximum' all fail the same orthographic test, and so would any verb in any subject matter. That is why '6.02 Liens.' separates from '6.02 The Company must deliver the report.' without the detector knowing anything about liens or reports.
genericRuleImplemented.lengthCeilingRemoved: the {0,80} body bound is gone; length never decides eligibility for scrutiny
genericRuleImplemented.scopeNote: The ALL-CAPS arm of the same caption test is untouched and remains a known-broken shape heuristic - out of scope by instruction, and now labelled as such in the code.
genericRuleImplemented.acceptedFalseReviews: A caption whose remainder carries a lowercase word ('6.02 Liens and encumbrances.') is now reported rather than dismissed. Per the trust-boundary architecture a false review is acceptable and a silently dropped covenant is not.

valuesAreHardSafetySignals.unchanged: The whole suppression block is still gated on values.length === 0, so a fragment carrying a recognised quantitative value can never receive HEADING_OR_LABEL. That guard was already correct and was not touched.
